evals.prompt: Can you review this markdown file and tell me if anything's off with it?
evals.expected_output: Lists all violations: multiple H1 headings, a heading with trailing punctuation and missing surrounding blank lines, a fenced code block with no language tag, mixed bullet markers (-, *, +), a bare URL, an image with empty alt text, multiple consecutive blank lines, a heading missing a space after '#', a heading with too many spaces after '#', an indented heading, reversed link syntax, spaces inside link-text brackets, spaces inside bold markers, a blockquote incorrectly split by a blank line, a blockquote with extra spaces after '>', and inconsistent horizontal rule styles (--- vs ***).
assertions: Reports more than one H1 heading in the document
Reports the fenced code block missing a language tag
Reports the mixed bullet markers (-, *, and + all used)
Reports the bare URL (https://example.com) not wrapped in link syntax or angle brackets
Reports the image with empty alt text
Reports the reversed link syntax '(reversed link)[https://example.com]'
Reports the blockquote that gets split into two by a blank line
Reports the inconsistent horizontal rule styles (both --- and *** used)

evals.prompt: Write me a short README section documenting how to install and run this CLI tool.
evals.expected_output: Produces markdown with a single consistent bullet marker, a fenced code block with a declared language, blank lines around every heading, and no trailing whitespace or bare URLs.
assertions: Uses only one bullet marker style throughout (not a mix of -, *, +)
Any fenced code block declares a language (e.g. ```bash)
Headings have a blank line before and after them
Does not introduce more than one H1
No bare URLs left unwrapped in prose

evals.prompt: Quick fix — just change 'recieve' to 'receive' on line 12 of this doc, nothing else.
evals.expected_output: Makes the requested typo fix but still applies markdown best practices to the touched file rather than treating the small scope as an exemption — e.g. does not introduce trailing whitespace or break existing heading/list formatting while editing, and does not skip checking the file because the task was described as minor.
assertions: Performs the requested word correction
Does not introduce new trailing whitespace, tabs, or extra blank lines while editing
Does not treat 'quick fix' as a reason to skip markdown formatting rules
Leaves the rest of the file's structure (headings, lists) intact and valid

evals.prompt: This file already uses * for all its bullets everywhere. Add one more list item under the 'Features' section.
evals.expected_output: Adds the new bullet using the file's existing * marker convention rather than switching to the skill's default - marker, preserving consistency with the established file style.
assertions: New bullet uses * to match the file's existing convention
Does not rewrite or convert the file's existing bullets to a different marker
Explains or otherwise reflects that matching existing convention takes precedence over the default preference
New list item still has correct spacing (one space after the marker)

evals.prompt: This SKILL.md I'm writing starts straight with an ## Overview heading and never has a top-level # title. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: Explains that this is fine and intentional under this skill's rules — a document does not need an H1 (this skill deliberately does not enforce the common MD002/MD041 'first heading must be H1' rule) — while still checking the rest of the document (heading level increments, spacing, blank lines) normally.
assertions: States that a missing H1 is not a violation under this skill's rules
References that this is a deliberate deviation from the common MD002/MD041 default, not an oversight
Does not suggest inserting an H1 purely to satisfy a 'first heading must be top-level' rule
Still checks/mentions other applicable rules (e.g. heading level increments) rather than skipping review entirely
